# A Chicago author-date sample

This fixture exercises the bare-year entry grammar: a year standing on its
own between periods, full given names instead of initials, and organisations
that end in a period rather than a comma. The in-text form is still
author-date, just without the comma.

## Method notes

Fieldwork was conducted across 2019 and 2020, and every transcript was coded
by hand. This paragraph mentions years without a period before them, so the
entry gate must not count it as a reference entry, however long it grows.

## Findings

The requirement-level vocabulary (Bradner 1997) predates agent security by
decades. Injection at scale was characterised by Greshake et al. (2023), and
the agent-level reformalisation followed (Debenedetti et al., 2024, pp. 4-6).
Two papers by one author in a single year appear as (Smith 2020a) and
(Smith 2020b), and a bare citation (Smith 2020) exercises the
suffix-ambiguity check. Anthropic (2024) documents the protocol itself. An
orphan citation appears here (Nonexistent, 2019).
